look_here_first: LOOK FIRST AT A NARROW, HAIRLESS LEAF and one TINY flower-like cyathium at the DISTAL NODE. E. golondrina is a prostrate annual with opposite narrow oblong leaves 5–11.5 × 1–4 mm, UNEQUAL bases, ENTIRE edges (no teeth) and mostly just the midvein showing. Inspect a cyathium with 10–20× magnification: four deeply concave, round RED–PURPLE glands and conspicuous WHITE crescent/fan-shaped appendages. Fruit is smooth, three-lobed and glabrous. The decisive close match is E. simulans: it has more ELLIPTIC gland shapes and normally lacks the white appendages, plus slightly larger 1.5–2 mm seeds. E. golondrina seed 1.3–1.5 mm, barely transversely ridged; seed and stipules require macro. Not an ordinary Hays County encounter plant: documented chiefly southwestern TX Rio Grande region. The current field photo shows narrow hairless leaves and tiny distal cyathia, but NOT microscopic mature seed ridges.

taxonomic_note: POWO/WCVP and Flora of North America accept Euphorbia golondrina L.C.Wheeler; Chamaesyce golondrina is a synonym. 'Golondrina' is also a common Spanish name for OTHER Euphorbia species (including E. hirta, E. thymifolia, E. hyssopifolia); never use common-name images as exact-species evidence.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae; Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum: opposite leaves, tiny specialized cyathia (not ordinary flowers), milky latex, three-lobed capsular fruit.
morphology_keys.habit: Annual with slender taproot. Prostrate slender stems 5–35 cm long, glabrous; in dry gravelly or sandy Rio Grande desert habitats. Do not call any single cropped shoot a whole rooted habit.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, oblong to ovate-oblong or narrowly elliptic-oblong, 5–11.5 × 1–4 mm; bases asymmetric/cuneate-to-rounded, tip blunt, MARGINS ENTIRE sometimes rolled under when dried; glabrous, prominent midvein only.
morphology_keys.stem_and_hairs: Stems, petioles, blades, involucres, capsules glabrous. Red-tinged stems are possible but not decisive.
morphology_keys.stipules: Distinct, slender awl-shaped (SUBULATE) 0.5–0.8 mm, hairless; microscopic true nodal attachment required to verify rather than an incidental hair.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Usually solitary at distal nodes; short peduncle 0.9–1.5 mm. Involucre turbinate and hairless 0.9–1.5 × 0.8–1.3 mm; 4 (occasionally rudimentary) DEEPLY CONCAVE SUBCIRCULAR glands, red–purple 0.3–0.4 mm with WHITE crescent to small fan-shaped appendages roughly 0.1–0.3 × 0.5–0.8 mm.
morphology_keys.capsule: Broadly ovoid 1.7–2 × 1.5–1.6 mm, GLABROUS. Do not confuse smooth capsule lobes with the brightly colored glands on separate cyathia.
morphology_keys.seed: Narrow pyramidal-ovoid, sharply 4-angled in cross section; 1.3–1.5 × 0.6–0.7 mm, very weak/faint transverse ribs or wrinkles.
best_field_traits: prostrate glabrous slender branches (5–35 cm) with tiny opposite entire-edged leaves
small oblong leaves 5–11.5 × 1–4 mm, only midvein prominent, asymmetric bases
solitary cyathia at distal nodes, round deeply cupped crimson-purple glands with clear white crescent-shaped appendages
1.3–1.5 mm mature 4-angled seeds with weak transverse ridges
E. simulans glands elliptic and without white appendages, 1.5–2 mm seeds; comparison best under hand lens

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against most likely close western FNA key partner E. simulans, compare the CIRCULAR deeply concave gland WITH white semilunate appendage of golondrina vs ELLIPTIC gland WITHOUT appendage in simulans; golondrina's mature seeds about 1.3–1.5 mm, simulans about 1.5–2 mm. E. serpens may be entirely smooth/hairless but roots at nodes, has BROAD fused triangular stipules, generally 0.7–1.1 mm SMOOTH seeds, and inconspicuous gland appendages. E. prostrata has hairy fruit keels and deeply transversely ribbed seeds. E. glyptosperma often has minutely serrulate leaf margins and irregular/fringed nodal stipules instead of golondrina's entire margin and distinct tiny awl-shaped stipules. All need enough structures for a secure determination.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Golondrina: narrow entire leaves, then the gland's white crescent
steps: FIRST: photograph slender prostrate shoot with a 5-cm scale and confirm leaves grow opposite.
SECOND: use a 10–20× loupe for the UNEQUAL leaf base, ENTIRE margins and hairless surface.
THIRD: locate solitary cyathium at distal node; get front and side macros of one gland, ideally showing DEEPLY CUPPED round red gland plus white semicircular appendage.
FOURTH: turn the leaf junction over for distinct AWL-LIKE stipules 0.5–0.8 mm with millimeter scale.
FIFTH: inspect an actual ripe smooth 3-lobed capsule and true seed at known magnification; seed ~1.3–1.5 mm and very weak cross-ridges.
SIXTH: if FNA's E. simulans possibility remains, compare gland outline, appendage presence, and seed size, not merely red stems or creeping habit.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: 'Golondrina' is an ambiguous folk name and online searches are full of E. hirta and other species. Use exact scientific identity, not plant-common-name photos. Cyathium appendage shape and mature seed sculpture require focused macro; the existing iNaturalist field shot alone doesn't prove these fine characters. Species associated with Big Bend/Rio Grande southwestern TX, not an assumed Hays native; county-native research intentionally deferred.
